'''Sharina Delores Person''' is an American [[biostatistics|biostatistician]] known for developing and directing the Diversity Engagement Survey of the [[Association of American Medical Colleges]]. She is a professor in the [[UMass Chan Medical School|University of Massachusetts Chan Medical School]], vice chair of the university's Department of Population and Quantitative Health Sciences, and Dr. Marcellette G. Williams Senior Scholar.{{r|profile}}

==Education and career==
Person is [[African-Americans|African-American]], and grew up with non-college-educated parents in a low-income and low-education neighborhood in [[Gary, Indiana]].{{r|statlife}}
She majored in mathematics and physics at the [[University of Alabama at Birmingham]], continuing there for a master's degree and Ph.D. in biostatistics.{{r|profile}} Her 1998 doctoral dissertation, ''The estimation and forecasting of incomplete stationary time series'', was supervised by J. Michael Hardin.{{r|diss}}

She became a faculty member at the University of Alabama at Birmingham before moving to the University of Massachusetts. {{r|profile}}

==Recognition==
In 2024 the University of Massachusetts Chan Medical School gave Person their Chancellor's Award for Advancing Institutional Excellence in Diversity and Inclusion.{{r|aix}} She was named as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 2026.{{r|fasa}}
